title: Two Taps on One Filter
endLine: Total arteriole resistance sets flow; the efferent share sets filter pressure.

scenes.tts: Each kidney filter sits between two tiny vessels. Squeeze the one that drains it, and filtration can rise or fall. Which, and why?
scenes.narration: Each kidney filter sits between two tiny vessels. Squeeze the one that drains it, and filtration can rise or fall. Which, and why?
scenes.caption: Each kidney filter sits between two tiny vessels. Squeeze the one that drains it, and filtration can rise or fall. Which, and why?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for both films (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene of both films: blood plasma flow RED dots; plasma protein PURPLE dots; water and filtrate CYAN drops; the afferent arteriole (inflow) a GREEN tube with a ring around it; the efferent arteriole (outflow) a YELLOW tube with a ring around it; the push line ORANGE; the pull line PURPLE (same as protein); Bowman's capsule and Bowman's space pale BLUE; all text WHITE at full opacity. Opening layout: in the centre, a rounded tuft of looping capillaries about 60% of frame height, sitting in a pale BLUE cup. A GREEN vessel enters the top of the cup from the left; a YELLOW vessel leaves it to the right. RED and PURPLE dots stream in on the left, loop through the tuft and leave on the right. CYAN drops drip steadily from the tuft into the cup and run off through a short outlet at its base. Motion during the line: on 'Squeeze the one that drains it', a pair of white pincers closes gently on the YELLOW vessel. The CYAN drip first quickens and a white up-arrow appears by the outlet; on 'or fall' the drip slows and a white down-arrow appears beside it; the two arrows flicker in turn. On the question, white text across the top: 'Rise or fall?'

Title 'Two Taps on One Filter' fades in above the tuft for 2 s. The pincers open and the drip returns to its starting rate; 'Rise or fall?' and the two arrows fade out beneath the title. Dots keep streaming through.

scenes.tts: The filter is a glomerulus, a tuft of capillaries cupped in Bowman's capsule. Plasma is pushed out through a wall of three layers. Water and small solutes pass freely. Plasma protein mostly stays behind.
scenes.narration: The filter is a glomerulus, a tuft of capillaries cupped in Bowman's capsule. Plasma is pushed out through a wall of three layers. Water and small solutes pass freely. Plasma protein mostly stays behind.
scenes.caption: The filter is a glomerulus, a tuft of capillaries cupped in Bowman's capsule. Plasma is pushed out through a wall of three layers. Water and small solutes pass freely. Plasma protein mostly stays behind.
scenes.visual: On 'glomerulus' the tuft glows and gets the label 'glomerulus'; on 'Bowman's capsule' the cup gets 'Bowman's capsule'. Then the tuft unwinds smoothly into ONE straight horizontal capillary across the middle of the frame, GREEN afferent tube on its left, YELLOW efferent tube on its right, and the blue cup flattens into a band directly beneath it labelled 'Bowman's space'. A small tag 'one capillary, schematic' sits at bottom right and stays. This straight-hose layout is the world for the rest of both films; it fills at least 60% of frame height once the strip above it appears in s04. On 'three layers', a round magnifier opens over one spot of the lower capillary wall and shows three plain stripes (no molecular detail) labelled 'fenestrated endothelium', 'basement membrane', 'podocyte slits'. On 'Water and small solutes', CYAN drops and tiny white specks slip through all three stripes; on 'protein mostly stays behind', PURPLE dots are turned back by the wall and stay in the tube. The magnifier closes.

scenes.tts: Filtrate leaves its protein behind. So the plasma flowing on carries the same protein in less water. Along the capillary, the protein grows more concentrated.
scenes.narration: Filtrate leaves its protein behind. So the plasma flowing on carries the same protein in less water. Along the capillary, the protein grows more concentrated.
scenes.caption: Filtrate leaves its protein behind. So the plasma flowing on carries the same protein in less water. Along the capillary, the protein grows more concentrated.
scenes.visual: CYAN drops leave the bottom of the straight capillary into Bowman's space along its length. The PURPLE protein dots stay in the tube and visibly crowd together from left to right: sparse at the GREEN end, densest at the YELLOW end. A faint PURPLE tint inside the tube deepens from left to right. Label above the right end of the tube: 'protein concentrates'. RED dots keep flowing left to right throughout.

scenes.tts: Picture two lines along the capillary. The push is the capillary's pressure, less a small back-pressure in Bowman's space. Between two arterioles, it stays nearly flat. The pull is the protein, holding water in. It starts lower and rises. Fluid filters wherever the push beats the pull.
scenes.narration: Picture two lines along the capillary. The push is the capillary's pressure, less a small back-pressure in Bowman's space. Between two arterioles, it stays nearly flat. The pull is the protein, holding water in. It starts lower and rises. Fluid filters wherever the push beats the pull.

scenes.visual: A strip of axes opens directly above the capillary, exactly as long as it, its horizontal axis lined up with the tube (left edge = afferent end, right edge = efferent end); vertical axis labelled 'mmHg', tag 'illustrative numbers'. On 'The push', an ORANGE line draws flat across the strip at 40, labelled 'push' (computed from the lesson's illustrative values: capillary 55 minus Bowman's space 15). On 'The pull', a PURPLE line starts at 25 at the left edge and climbs to the right, rising steepest at the left and flattening as it goes (this shape is schematic), staying below the orange line in this scene; label 'pull'. The gap between the two lines fills pale CYAN, labelled 'net filtration'; at the left edge it is 15 tall. On 'wherever the push beats the pull', the CYAN drops leaving the tube below thicken where the shaded gap above is widest and thin out to the right, column by column in step with the shading.

scenes.tts: If enough water leaves, the pull rises to meet the push before the far end. Beyond that point, nothing filters. In mildly water-deprived rats, the pull typically caught up. Whether human glomeruli do is unknown.
scenes.narration: If enough water leaves, the pull rises to meet the push before the far end. Beyond that point, nothing filters. In mildly water-deprived rats, the pull typically caught up. Whether human glomeruli do is unknown.
scenes.caption: If enough water leaves, the pull rises to meet the push before the far end. Beyond that point, nothing filters. In mildly water-deprived rats, the pull typically caught up. Whether human glomeruli do is unknown.
scenes.visual: The PURPLE pull line steepens and touches the ORANGE push line about two-thirds of the way along (position schematic), then runs along it to the right edge. A WHITE dot marks the meeting point, labelled 'equilibrium'. To the right of the dot the cyan shading vanishes and no drops fall from that stretch of tube: it stays dry while red and purple dots keep flowing through it. On 'rats', a small rat silhouette blinks in beside the dot with a white tick; on 'human glomeruli', a small human silhouette appears with a white '?' and no tick. Both silhouettes fade out at the end of the scene.

scenes.tts: So filtration depends on two things. How high the pressure is. And how much plasma flows through, which slows the concentrating of the protein.
scenes.narration: So filtration depends on two things. How high the pressure is. And how much plasma flows through, which slows the concentrating of the protein.
scenes.caption: So filtration depends on two things. How high the pressure is. And how much plasma flows through, which slows the concentrating of the protein.
scenes.visual: On 'How high the pressure is', the ORANGE push line pulses and a white label 'pressure' appears at its left end. On 'how much plasma flows through', a broad RED arrow appears inside the tube pointing right, the red dots brighten, and a white label 'flow' appears under the arrow. The red arrow and the 'flow' label stay for the rest of the film. Do not move the equilibrium dot in this scene; drops keep falling at the same pattern as before.

scenes.tts: Blood enters through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole. Picture a hose: a tap near the spigot, a nozzle at the far end, and a leaky stretch between.
scenes.narration: Blood enters through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole. Picture a hose: a tap near the spigot, a nozzle at the far end, and a leaky stretch between.
scenes.caption: Blood enters through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole. Picture a hose: a tap near the spigot, a nozzle at the far end, and a leaky stretch between.
scenes.visual: Camera eases back just enough that both arterioles and the whole capillary fit, with the strip still above. On 'afferent arteriole', the GREEN tube at left brightens and gets the label 'afferent: in'; on 'efferent arteriole', the YELLOW tube at right brightens and gets 'efferent: out'. On 'a tap near the spigot', the ring on the green tube grows a small tap handle; on 'a nozzle', the ring on the yellow tube becomes a nozzle; on 'a leaky stretch', the dripping capillary pulses once. The tap and nozzle shapes stay for both films.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. The two arterioles set both pressure and flow. Their total resistance sets the flow. The efferent share of that resistance sets the pressure left in the filter. So the afferent moves pressure and flow the same way. The efferent moves them opposite ways.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. The two arterioles set both pressure and flow. Their total resistance sets the flow. The efferent share of that resistance sets the pressure left in the filter. So the afferent moves pressure and flow the same way. The efferent moves them opposite ways.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. The two arterioles set both pressure and flow. Their total resistance sets the flow. The efferent share of that resistance sets the pressure left in the filter. So the afferent moves pressure and flow the same way. The efferent moves them opposite ways.
scenes.visual: The lesson's round numbers appear small in white: 'arterial 100' at the far left inflow and 'venous 10' at the far right outflow (both mmHg), and '1 unit' on each ring. Beside the red arrow: 'flow 45 units'; at the left end of the orange push line: 'capillary 55' (the push line still sits at 55 minus 15 = 40). These come from the lesson: (100 - 10) / (1 + 1) = 45, and 10 + 90 x 1/2 = 55. On 'total resistance sets the flow', both rings glow together and a white bracket spans them, label 'total sets flow'. On 'efferent share', only the YELLOW ring glows, label 'share sets pressure'. On 'the afferent moves pressure and flow the same way', the GREEN tap tightens briefly: the red arrow thins and the orange line drops together (arrows only, no new numbers, tag 'schematic directions'), then the tap relaxes back. On 'opposite ways', the YELLOW nozzle tightens briefly: the red arrow thins while the orange line rises, then the nozzle relaxes back to the starting state.

scenes.tts: Now squeeze the efferent arteriole harder, and harder again. The pressure in the filter keeps climbing. Does filtration keep climbing with it?
scenes.narration: Now squeeze the efferent arteriole harder, and harder again. The pressure in the filter keeps climbing. Does filtration keep climbing with it?
scenes.caption: Now squeeze the efferent arteriole harder, and harder again. The pressure in the filter keeps climbing. Does filtration keep climbing with it?
scenes.visual: The round-number labels fade. The YELLOW nozzle tightens in three slow steps. With each step the ORANGE push line rises one notch, the RED dots slow and the red arrow thins. The drops under the tube and the purple line stay as they are (no answer shown). Question card in white across the top: 'Harder squeeze, more filtration?'

Predict pause. The question card 'Harder squeeze, more filtration?' stays. Near-stillness by design: red dots creep slowly through the tube, drops fall at an even rate, the nozzle holds at its third step, the orange line shimmers faintly.

scenes.tts: Not forever. Each squeeze also cuts the flow. With less plasma passing, the protein concentrates sooner, so the pull catches up earlier. And the pressure can never exceed arterial pressure, so its gain levels off.
scenes.narration: Not forever. Each squeeze also cuts the flow. With less plasma passing, the protein concentrates sooner, so the pull catches up earlier. And the pressure can never exceed arterial pressure, so its gain levels off.
scenes.caption: Not forever. Each squeeze also cuts the flow. With less plasma passing, the protein concentrates sooner, so the pull catches up earlier. And the pressure can never exceed arterial pressure, so its gain levels off.
scenes.visual: The card dissolves. The nozzle keeps tightening slowly. On 'cuts the flow', the red arrow thins further and the red dots slow. On 'the protein concentrates sooner', purple dots crowd earlier along the tube, the PURPLE pull line steepens, and the WHITE equilibrium dot slides left toward the afferent end; the dry stretch of tube to its right grows. On 'never exceed arterial pressure', a dashed WHITE line labelled 'arterial pressure' appears near the top of the strip; the ORANGE push line rises toward it in ever smaller steps and flattens out beneath it, never touching it. All shapes schematic.

scenes.tts: So a mild squeeze raises filtration slightly. A hard squeeze lowers it from its peak. Throughout, a larger share of the plasma is filtered: the filtration fraction rises.
scenes.narration: So a mild squeeze raises filtration slightly. A hard squeeze lowers it from its peak. Throughout, a larger share of the plasma is filtered: the filtration fraction rises.
scenes.caption: So a mild squeeze raises filtration slightly. A hard squeeze lowers it from its peak. Throughout, a larger share of the plasma is filtered: the filtration fraction rises.
scenes.visual: The strip above the tube morphs in place into a small graph: horizontal axis 'efferent squeeze', vertical axis unlabelled, tag 'schematic'. The nozzle replays from relaxed to hard while a CYAN curve labelled 'filtration' draws in step: a slight rise, a rounded peak, then a fall from the peak that stays above its starting level in the drawn range. The drops under the tube quicken a little, then slow, matching the curve. On 'filtration fraction rises', a WHITE line labelled 'filtration fraction' draws across the same axes, climbing steadily the whole way.

scenes.tts: That is the answer to the opening puzzle. Filtering needs push to beat pull. The arterioles' combined resistance decides how much plasma arrives. Where that resistance sits decides how hard it is pushed.
scenes.narration: That is the answer to the opening puzzle. Filtering needs push to beat pull. The arterioles' combined resistance decides how much plasma arrives. Where that resistance sits decides how hard it is pushed.
scenes.caption: That is the answer to the opening puzzle. Filtering needs push to beat pull. The arterioles' combined resistance decides how much plasma arrives. Where that resistance sits decides how hard it is pushed.
scenes.visual: The nozzle relaxes to its starting setting and the graph morphs back into the push-and-pull strip in its starting shape (orange flat at 40, purple rising from 25, cyan gap between). On 'push to beat pull', the cyan gap pulses. On 'combined resistance', both rings glow and the red arrow pulses. On 'Where that resistance sits', a glow slides from the GREEN ring to the YELLOW ring and the orange line pulses. Drops keep falling.

End card over the dimmed but still moving hose world, large white text, centred: 'Total arteriole resistance sets flow; the efferent share sets filter pressure.' Red dots creep through the capillary and cyan drops fall gently behind the line.
